newsitem.title: UK: British schoolboy returns from bout of wanderlust.
newsitem.headline: British schoolboy returns from bout of wanderlust.

text.p: Britain's most famous runaway schoolboy returned to his London home on Monday after being picked up by German police cycling along an autobahn, local news agencies said.

Peter Kerry, 15, had been missing from his home for a week since setting off for his part-time job delivering newspapers on a Sunday morning. Last year, he left home after a family row and flew to Malaysia, using his father's passport and credit card. It took a six-day international police search to trace him.

Newspapers said the six-feet (two-metre) tall schoolboy had been hoping to cycle to Budapest when he was found in Germany on Sunday. "There's no logical explanation other than he wants to see the world," his father, John Kerry, told reporters.

A court gave Kerry a 12-month conditional discharge after he admitted eight charges following his trip to Malaysia. He had altered the photograph and date of birth on his father's passport and used the credit card to pay for flights and hotels.
Kerry has also taken himself on trips to Scotland and Paris.
